newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Lower interest rates boost Zimbabwe shares.
newsitem.headline: Lower interest rates boost Zimbabwe shares.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares rose 2.5 percent on Tuesday with brokers saying the local bourse was getting a boost from local investors deserting the money market where interest rates have been falling steadily over the months.

The key industrial index soared 170.20 points to end the day at 7,011.30, pushed up mainly by blue-chip conglomerate Delta's 100-cent jump to 3,200, clothing retailer Edgars' 250-cent leap to 3,000 and merchant banker FMB's 125-cent rise to 125.
"The market was very strong today. Low interest rates on the money market are driving investors to the stock market," one broker said.

Short-term interest rates on the local money market have fallen to the lower 20s from around 30 percent in January on increased liquidity and due to a softening in annual inflation which is currently pegged at a three-year low of 17.7 percent from a peak of 28 percent in January.

Brokers said Standard Chartered Bank Zimbabwe's lowering on Monday of its minimum lending rate to 28.5 percent from 30 percent and hopes that other banks would follow suit could also see more local institutional investors flowing to the stock market.
"As long as rates continue coming down, the market will continue to gain," one broker said.

Among the winners on Tuesday, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans rose 100 cents to 3,200, clothing retailer Truworths gained 50 cents to 650 as did timber producer Border to 1,300, bankers Barclays jumped 40 cents to 2,000, while farming implement-maker Zimplow and winery Afdis added 30 cents each to 350 and 400 respectively.
There were only two losers, cable manufacturer BICAF which lost 10 cents to 390 and tyre trader NTS which shed 15 cents to 435.

Minings were quieter with copper producer Mhangura firming three cents to 19 while Falgold added five cents to 140. However, nickel company Bindura dropped 25 cents to 1,100, leaving the mining index 1.61 points lower at 1,244.09.
